items.title: A fast path's paired held-out comparison runs as the check of a change to that path, never in every measurement run

steps.title: A fast path's paired held-out comparison runs as the check of a change to that path, never in every measurement run
steps.rationale: SQA-266 (P1, the lane part). The 2026-10-31 run's model suites (cmd/validate lane walls) took 304 minutes of test time, 237 of them in four paired held-out comparisons: TestQwen35CellsHoldHeldOut 105, TestFlashNextSpeculationHoldsIFEval 49, TestKQuantProductsHoldHeldOut 42, TestAttentionCellsHoldHeldOut 41. Each answers whole MMLU-Pro, IFEval or BBH parts twice, a fast path and its reference, and each was the check of the change that made its path (263d0eecb, f3219a174, 4b25f6d1c, 599de6efd). go test's cache replays a package nothing changed, but internal/evaluation builds on internal/inference, which changes between nearly every pair of runs (16 of the 99 packages its tests build on between the 2026-10-30 and 2026-10-31 runs), so the four ran whole every run. The served path's held-out quality is measured by the run's cells every run, to the digit. The change: the four build only under the tag pairtest, which no lane builds and vet reads, and a step that changes the path one compares names it in its verify.

items.title: The loop finishes: no run of every model while the plan holds work, each step judged by its own check or its own model, one run at the end

steps.title: A run of every model starts only when the plan is empty, a run left one unfinished or none has completed, a hand start included
steps.rationale: SQA-267 (P1, its part 0). The owner on 2026-10-31: rerunning the whole scorecard after every fix is wrong, neither the doctrine nor the automation asks for it, and the lead is to stop retesting the entire scorecard indefinitely without finishing. The automation starts a cycle when the plan empties or when landings that moved what it measures reach a limit (cmd/loop CycleDue), but no limit is set and the plan never empties, so it starts none, and the lead started both runs of 2026-10-31 by hand with go run ./cmd/loop -improve, which asked nothing: the second after a fix to three records whose own checks had passed on the card, an 8-hour run for it. The change: -improve asks HandStartDue and refuses, saying why, unless the plan is empty, a run left a cycle unfinished, or no cycle has completed. A fix is judged by its own check, and a decline by its own model's cells (model-cells).

steps.title: One model's cells are measured alone, so a decline's row is judged without a run of every model
steps.rationale: The rows a scorecard files for a declined cell carry the check go run ./cmd/validate -scorecard -gap <key> -target <value>, which reads the store's newest readings (openGap, scorecard.Build), but validate -run measures every model's cells or none, so each such row could close only on a run of every model, about 8 hours, and that run filed the next rows. The change: validate -run -cells -model <name> measures the named model's cells alone into the store, as the cycle measures them (the same commands, attempts and medians), so the gap check reads the decline's own model measured again in minutes.

steps.title: A cell whose inputs are unchanged since its last reading is credited with it, not measured again
steps.rationale: SQA-266 (P1, the cell part): SelectValidation schedules every active cell, 110 on 2026-10-31, as re-acquired every cycle, so a change to one model measures all of them again, and a held-out benchmark reuses an answer only where the code that answers now gave it, so a change anywhere in internal/inference answers every suite again. The 2026-10-30 scorecard's readings name 45 code commits, so some are kept already. Measure first which cells the 2026-10-31 run measured again although their model files, the execution identity of the code they run, the device and the driver were those of their last reading, and what they cost. The change: such a cell is credited with that reading, labelled unchanged since its scorecard, and a change to code every model runs measures them all again.

steps.title: A worsened cell whose model, recipe and code identity are unchanged is reported, not filed as a row
steps.rationale: SQA-267 (P1, the finish line): each published scorecard files a row for every cell worse than its earlier readings past its noise allowance, so the run that confirms a finished plan can file rows from noise on code that changed nothing the cell reads, and the plan never empties. A decline is filed only when something the cell reads changed since the reading it is compared with, and otherwise it is printed as a reading beside its allowance. A reading names its commit, not the identity of the code it ran (scorecard Cell code_commit), so this step builds on the identity each reading records for cell-credit.

items.title: A filing beside the review session's uncommitted findings is still a filing

steps.title: A change to the plan and the findings register alone lands as a filing, carrying the register
steps.rationale: On 2026-10-31 the filing of paired-comparisons and finish-line was refused (paired-comparisons/file is not a step of the plan at e63fd568a467 ... land the plan's edit alone first), because docs/sqa_findings.json held SQA-266 to SQA-268, which the guard refused the review session's commit of: a change counts as the plan's alone only when no other path changes (planOnly, internal/landing/landing.go:363), so while the register is dirty no row can be filed, and it is dirty after every review. The owner on 2026-10-31: a review session writes its findings into docs/sqa_findings.json itself, and when the guard refuses its commit the edit stays saved and its commit is the lead's call. The filing went in with the landing of a decline row its check closed. A change to the plan and the register alone is judged as a filing, by the plan it holds, and carries the register; any other path makes it a change judged by the terms its row had before it, as now. Serves: the loop, which can file the rows a run or a request needs whenever a review has run.

items.title: Implement the MOSS transformer in the native graph

budget.reason: Missing text refinement, shared modulation and bounded SITU arithmetic are expected; reuse existing attention, normalization, linear and graph kernels.

steps.title: Match transformer arithmetic and branch skipping
steps.rationale:

steps.title: Flash-Next's 16,384-token prompt read comes back to its 2026-10-25 first output, toward Strata's
steps.rationale: Split from flashnext-first-request on 2026-10-30, whose first output and throughput are met and whose load is declared a trade. The 16,384-token first output reads 6.2 s against 5563.9 ms on 2026-10-25, and Strata reads the same prompt in 4.94 to 5.04 s (the reviewer's bench, scratchpad round/alt62): the read takes 5.85 s and the round's setup after it 0.34 s. Measured on the served model: the n-gram embedding's rows for the read are fetched from the model file in two loads of 131,072 rows, 0.26 s on the read's path before its chunks run (inference feedNGramInputs, model.HostRows); the rest is the chunks' MoE products on the card and the host experts' on the CPU (hostexpert, about 2.5 s of CPU over the read). First suspects, each measured before it is changed: the n-gram rows fetched for the next chunk while the current one runs; the host experts' share of a long read, against where Strata's read computes them; and the chunk size a long read takes.

items.title: Load and resolve only the kernels a model's graphs launch, so a first request pays for its own

steps.title: Load each kernel module, and resolve each function, when a graph first launches from it
steps.rationale: Every model's first request runs the executor's setup (ensureResources): loading the three kernel modules from PTX (ops_f32 6.1 MB, strata_qsa 4.4 MB, strata_native 2.5 MB; about 6, 8 and 5 ms each with the driver's compiled cache warm) and resolving all 446 functions, then setting the large-shared kernels' limits, about 30 ms of a first request in a CPU profile. The Strata decode port added strata_native and with it 13 ms to Qwen3.5-9B's first request on a fresh load (44 to 57 ms at 8cc359407, each read twice); Qwen2.5-0.5B's measured attempts stepped 115 to 131 ms across the same window. After cells-first-request (the cell layers' needless cuBLAS, about 70 ms) and first-request-setup (the bundle's hash, about 5 ms), the first-output rows still stand above their targets on fresh measurements from a clean tree: Bonsai-27B 120 ms (target 102.7), Qwen3.5-9B 54 ms (39.1), Qwen2.5-0.5B 129 to 132 ms (125); gemma-4-E4B-it read 200 and 311 ms, its first request reading its weights back after the other models' loads. The change loads a module, and resolves a function, only when a graph first launches from it, before the graph runs or is captured, so a model pays for the kernels it uses: most models never launch the native module's 70 functions or the QSA module's 123. The launches index the function table directly in many hand-written files and setup configures some functions up front, so the change is mechanical but wide. The check is set before the code lands, with the test that holds it.

Now, ahead of such a candidate
